Guljan Bewa & Others ------ Petitioner
Vs.
Hakim Uddin Sarker & Others ------ Respondent
full_judgment:
S.M. Husain, J: A land was allegedly transferred by two village women being the mother and the daughter in favour of defendant Nos.1 and 2 by a registered deed of conveyance. Such transfer was challenged claiming under pre-emption by defendant No.3. Thereafter the alleged executants and vendors filed a suit for cancellation of such registered deed of conveyance allegedly to have been obtained fraudulently without passing any consideration. In such suit vendees being defendant Nos. 1 and 2 were made necessary parties against whom fraud was alleged in obtaining registered deed of conveyance in their favour. Defendant No.3 claiming the land in pre-emption was added as a proper party whose presence was necessary for the disposal of the suit. Before the trial court the defendant Nos.1 and 2 against whom fraud was alleged in obtaining a registered deed of conveyance from the plaintiff, though filed written statement but did not further appear in court to depose in the suit and to contest the case. Defendant No.3 being the pre-emptor of the land in question however entered appearance and contested the suit. The trial court upon consideration of the evidence on record found that the registered deed of conveyance was obtained by the defendant Nos.1 and 2 fraudulently without passing any consideration. The trial court decreed the suit ex parte against the defendant Nos.1 and 2 and on contest against the defendant No.3 The defendant Nos. 1 and 2 against whom an ex parte decree was passed by the trial court holding that they obtained a registered deed of conveyance fraudulently without consideration, neither applied for setting aside of the ex parte decree passed against them nor preferred any appeal. The defendant No.3 as the pre-emptor however preferred an appeal. The lower appellate court set aside the judgment of the trial court and dismissed the plaintiff's suit against which the present second appeal was preferred before this court. 

 2. The present suit for cancellation of a registered deed of convyeance was principally and primarily directed against the vendees to the document against whom, fraud was alleged. As such defendant Nos.1 and 2 did not file any appearance before the trial court to contest the suit and it was decreed exparte against them. Such defendant Nos. 1 and 2 also did not file any proceeding for setting aside of the exparte decree and also did not make any appeal challenging the exparte decree passed against them by the trial .court cancelling the registered deed of conveyance. Consequently the plaintiff's allegation of obtaining registered deed of conveyance fraudulently without consideration by the defendant Nos. 1 and 2 stood uncontested and unchallenged at any stage by such defendant Nos. 1 and 2. The suit was contested all through only by defendant No.3 Who was claiming the land in question under pre-emption and was not at all a party to the registered deed of conveyance sought to be cancelled. It is well established principal of law that a third party who is not otherwise a party to any transaction made through a registered document cannot challenge the legality and validity of such registered document. Once the trial court found that the registered deed of conveyance was obtained from the plaintiff  fraudulently without consideration by defendant Nos. 1 and 2 who never finally appeared in the suit to contest the case and never applied to set aside the exparte decree and never preferred any appeal, the defendant No.3 who was mere proper party in the suit being not a party to the registered document sought to be cancelled, could not prefer any appeal without the concurrence of the defendant Nos. 1 and 2. Thus the exparte decree passed by the trial court against defendant Nos. 1 and 2 remaining Unchallenged by such defendant Nos. 1 and 2, no appeal could be preferred at the instance of defendant No.3 in a suit for cancellation of a registered document to which such defendant No.3 was not a party. In such circumstances the appeal preferred before the lower appellate court by defendant No.3 was incompetent and consequently the lower appellate court illegally dismissed the plaintiff's case. 

 3. In this connection it may be observed that since the defendant No.3 was claiming the suit land under pre-emption and was not a party to the registered deed of conveyance which has been challenged in this suit, such defendant No. 3 was a mere proper party in this present suit in whose presence the suit was required to be disposed of. There being no legal claim against the defendant No.3 being a popper party, no binding decree could be passed against the said defendant No.3. The trail court wrongly passed such decree against the defendant No.3. 

 4. In that view of the case, the judgment and decree passed by the lower appellate court is set aside and the judgment and decree passed by the trial court is restored. The plaintiff's suit against defendant No.1 and 2 stands decreed exparte and the registered deed of conveyance stands cancelled. The plaintiff's suit against defendant No.3 who is not a party to the registered deed of conveyance is however dismissed. The appeal is allowed accordingly. There will be no order as to cost.
